name: Cheesy Fried Shallot Burger Stacks with Lemony Asparagus & Peppers
instructions: Peel, halve, and slice shallots into very thin half-moons. Place in a small bowl and sprinkle with salt; using your hands, massage the shallot until it starts to soften. Set aside.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Snap or cut off the woody ends of the asparagus; trim, seed, and slice bell peppers into thin strips. Transfer both to a large baking sheet pan, spreading them out in an even layer.
Peel and mince garlic. Sprinkle garlic over the veggies and drizzle with oil. Squeeze lemon over top, then season with salt and pepper.
Place veggies in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until crisp-tender, 12-15 minutes. Remove from the oven.
While the veggies are roasting, grate cheese into a medium bowl.
Add beef and spices to the bowl with the cheese; mix with your hands until well combined. Form the beef mixture into 8 equal-sized patties and place on a plate.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, use paper towels or a clean cloth to squeeze excess moisture out of the shallots. Divide shallots into 8 portions, then press into the top of each burger patty.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add patties, shallot-side down, and cook, undisturbed, until shallots are golden, about 4 minutes.

Using a metal spatula, carefully slide underneath the shallots and flip the patties (place any loose shallots back on top of the burgers); cook an additional 3-4 minutes, until cooked through. Once done, transfer to a clean plate.
Meanwhile, slice each tomato crosswise into 4 rounds.
Divide roasted veggies and tomato slices between plates; top each tomato slice with a burger patty. Enjoy!
author: Mealime
